# Bulwark

> Bulwark is free, open-source (Apache-2.0), local-first security for developers and their AI coding agents: a native CLI (`bulwarkctl`, installed as `bulwark` by the desktop package) and a Tauri desktop app on one Rust engine, for Linux, macOS and Windows. It scans the AI coding assistants on a machine (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, Codex, Gemini and about twenty more) for configuration a prompt injection or poisoned repository could turn into code execution — project-supplied hooks, auto-approve and never-ask modes, a disabled sandbox, MCP servers on unpinned packages or a vulnerable mcp-remote, hidden-Unicode instruction files, API base-URL overrides — and for keys leaked into session transcripts and memory, which it can remove with a backup. It then checks the machine itself against 100 declarative rules: plaintext credential stores (AWS, Git, Docker, npm, PyPI, kube), developer-tool settings that switch security off (Git TLS and safe.directory, SSH host-key checks and agent forwarding, unverified npm/pip registries, an unauthenticated Docker API), Python startup hooks and supply-chain indicators, dev services exposed on all interfaces, the host firewall, SSH, sudoers, kernel hardening, persistence, file permissions, logging and rootkit indicators. Every finding is explained in plain language with a concrete fix, and every check has its own page at https://bulwark.nrl.ai/checks/. A check that couldn't run is reported as such, never counted as a pass. It can also watch other machines over plain SSH — agentless, host keys verified, an unreachable machine never reported as clean — with optional Telegram or e-mail alerts. No telemetry. Website: https://bulwark.nrl.ai — Source: https://github.com/vietanhdev/bulwark

## Key facts

- License: Apache-2.0. Free and open source.
- Platforms: Linux x86_64 and aarch64 (Ubuntu 22.04+, Debian 12+, Fedora 36+). Ships as .deb, .rpm, and AppImage. Also runs natively on macOS (FileVault, Gatekeeper, SIP, firewall, automatic security updates, guest account, launchd persistence, plus the credential and SSH-key checks) and Windows (Defender, firewall, BitLocker, UAC, Remote Desktop, SMBv1). Inside WSL, Linux checks that concern the Windows host (its kernel, network stack, console) are reported as not applicable. Remote monitoring over SSH covers Linux (including WSL), macOS and Windows.
- Built with: Rust, Tauri v2, React. One engine (`bulwark-core`), two front-doors (CLI + desktop app).
- Privacy: local-first, no telemetry, no network calls from the core; scan history in a local SQLite database. The only network use is opt-in and user-directed: SSH to machines you register, and alerts to your own Telegram bot or SMTP server.
- Rules are data (YAML) with a small condition DSL — adding a check needs no Rust and no recompile.

## Documentation

- [Download](https://bulwark.nrl.ai/download): install for Debian/Ubuntu, Fedora/RHEL, or any distro (AppImage).
- [Architecture](https://bulwark.nrl.ai/guide/architecture): the engine, data model, and design decisions.
- [AI agent security](https://bulwark.nrl.ai/guide/agent-security): how Bulwark scans AI coding assistants, and the 23 AI-security checks (mapped to CVEs / MITRE ATT&CK).
- [Fixing findings](https://bulwark.nrl.ai/guide/remediation): how remediation works.
- [Monitoring other machines](https://bulwark.nrl.ai/guide/remote-monitoring): agentless SSH monitoring, connection security, scheduling, and Telegram/e-mail alerts.
